question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=\sqrt{g},\,g=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{g}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{g}}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}}.\end{aligned}
$$
